answer_text: Yes, by its own account. 1Password says an attacker got into an employee's GitHub account, reached some backend systems and copied names, email addresses and account details for some customers. It says password vaults were not touched.
label: Confirmed

question_text: Were my 1Password passwords or vault exposed?
answer_text: Not according to 1Password. It says vault contents, and the keys that protect them, were never available to the attacker, and that it does not hold account passwords or Secret Keys. Nobody outside the company has checked this.
label: Reported

question_text: Do I need to change my 1Password password?
answer_text: 1Password says no: customers do not need to update anything. It asks them to be wary of unexpected emails about 1Password invitations or account recovery.
label: Reported

what_would_settle_it: 1Password giving a number or sending notices to affected customers.

question_text: How did the attacker get into the employee's GitHub account?
what_would_settle_it: 1Password or its outside investigators explaining how the account was taken over.

question_text: Did the attacker tamper with the 1Password apps or browser extension?
answer_text: 1Password says no: its apps and browser extensions were not affected, and the attacker's code went to backend services. Nobody outside the company has checked.
label: Reported

question_text: Was the attacker's code pushed with no code review?
answer_text: Not established. 1Password has not said how the code reached its servers or what checks it passed. The claim comes from commenters online, not from anyone with knowledge of it.

question_text: Can the attacker use a copied recovery link to get into my account?
answer_text: Not on its own, 1Password says: the token in the link also needs a single sign-on login or a code sent to your email. It says it has seen no account taken over this way.
label: Reported

question_text: Which organisations use 1Password, and were they affected?
answer_text: 1Password's own customer pages name Canva, Asana, DigitalOcean, JetBrains and Elastic among the organisations that use it. None of them, and no other organisation, has said it was affected, and 1Password has named no affected customer.
